newsitem.title: UK: Provident Financial to consider shr buyback.
newsitem.headline: Provident Financial to consider shr buyback.

text.p: British credit and insurance group Provident Financial Plc said on Thursday it would continue to consider growth by acquisition and a possible share buyback as a way to improve shareholder value. The company also said its chairman, Antony Warde-Norbury, would retire at the annual general meeting.
John van Kuffeler, currently deputy chairman and chief executive, will take up the position of executive chairman, the company said in a statement.
Provident said Howard Bell, currently group managing director, would become chief executive.
The company also said it would strengthen its board by recruiting two more non-executive directors.

"We will also continue to consider the shareholders' long-term interests by regularly evaluating suitable opportunities for expansion of the group by acquisition and the merits of a share buyback or other ways of improving value for shareholders," Provident said.
Provident posted a 17 percent rise in its 1996 pretax profits to 118.5 million stg and added that it had made a good start to 1997.
"The board is confident that the management will again meet all the challenges of the new financial year and will continue to improve the company's performance," it said.
